title: 01 Bach

sections.title: J.S. Bach: Counterpoint and Dance Forms

blocks.text: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) worked in German churches and courts, composing fugues, chorales, suites, and partitas central to Western music education.

The Well-Tempered Clavier (48 preludes and fugues in all keys) demonstrated equal-temperament keyboard writing. Brandenburg Concertos showcase Baroque orchestration. Cello Suites and violin Partitas remain performance staples.
Bach absorbed allemandes, courantes, sarabandes, and gigues into instrumental suites — linking court music to European dance tradition.
Two-part invention shows bass implying harmony while melody sings — same split session guitarists use. Ornament tables influence baroque-influenced flute and harp gracing.

- A) Preludes and fugues in all keys
- B) Inventing tin whistle
- C) Jazz standards only
- D) Electric guitar

**Answer:** A

sections.title: Q2. Bach used dance forms like gigues in suites.

quiz_markdown:
### Q1. Well-Tempered Clavier famous for:

- A) Preludes and fugues in all keys
- B) Inventing tin whistle
- C) Jazz standards only
- D) Electric guitar

**Answer:** A

### Q2. Bach used dance forms like gigues in suites.

**Answer:** True
